message.reasoning:
I am preparing to respond as a Monopoly player.

Evaluating p3's offer of $290 for KENTUCKY_AVENUE against my holdings and the board state.

Verifying standard Monopoly property colors to confirm the red set. Tennessee Avenue is orange, not red.

Confirmed the full color distribution. The red set is split three ways: Indiana (p1), Illinois (p3), and Kentucky (me). The orange set includes Tennessee (p3) and New York (p4).

The $290 offer is $70 above the $220 list price. Completing two of three reds would give p3 a major strategic advantage and likely prompt them to bid aggressively for Indiana. Selling Kentucky would leave me cash-rich but remove my red foothold.

Rejecting the offer is the better move. Selling Kentucky would let p3 assemble a red monopoly with just Indiana, concentrating power against me. I should counter with something that benefits me more, such as trading for one of p3's properties.

P3 would not trade Illinois cheaply. Tennessee cannot complete a set without New York and St. James. A counter offer for Illinois plus cash is too risky. The best move is to reject the trade and keep Kentucky as a blocking piece.

A counter offer swapping Kentucky for Illinois would be useless. I would still only own one red. I should try to buy Illinois from p3 instead.

A straight swap for Illinois would be unbalanced. Illinois is worth more and pays higher rent than Kentucky.

Offering cash for Illinois is another option. A fair price might be $350 to $450. That would give me two reds and leave me with about $588 cash. I would still need Indiana from p1 to complete the set.

P1 recently rejected a $300 offer for Indiana. They want property-for-property swaps instead.

A property-for-property swap for Indiana would give p1 two pinks and leave Virginia unowned. That is risky because p1 could land on Virginia to complete the set. Reds are more valuable than pinks.

The current offer of $290 for Kentucky should be rejected outright.

I will not counter with a new offer. Signaling interest in a trade could reveal my strategy.

I will reject the offer without hostility. I will not reveal that I am holding Kentucky specifically to block p3. A counter asking for Illinois plus cash would be aggressive and waste an exchange.

I will keep Kentucky as a blocking piece. The only scenario where I would sell it is if the cash were high enough to buy greens or yellows from the bank. I will decline the offer without over-explaining.
